must_remember: The forbidden energy gap ($E_g$) in insulators is large, typically greater than $3 \text{ eV}$.
Electrical conductivity ($\sigma$) of insulators ranges from $10^{-10}$ to $10^{-20} \text{ } \Omega^{-1} \text{ m}^{-1}$.
The temperature coefficient of resistance for insulators is negative due to thermally activated carrier generation.
Total polarizability is the sum of electronic, ionic, and orientational polarizabilities: $\alpha = \alpha_e + \alpha_i + \alpha_o$.
Dielectric breakdown occurs when an electric field exceeds the critical dielectric strength threshold, causing heavy conduction.

glossary.meaning: The highest range of electron energies in which electrons are present at absolute zero ($0 \text{ K}$) temperature.
The lowest range of vacant electronic energy states that lie above the valence band.
An energy range in a solid where no electron wave states can exist, separating the valence and conduction bands.
The relative permittivity of a material, determining its energy storage capacity through polarization in an electric field.
A form of electrical breakdown caused by cumulative impact ionization from high-velocity free electrons.
